unstated.what: Import location of the new Transformer class must be the same module as the other override parser types (so `from ...overrides_parser.types import Transformer` resolves); the instruction leaves naming/placement "up to you".
`sweep_iterator` must accept the element as keyword argument named `transformer`.
Exact keyword name `transformer=` on the new sweep_iterator API
Transformer.encode must return list/dict/quoted-string elements flattened to the exact existing string form (e.g. "[1,1.1,'2','a']", "'a','b'") while returning primitives natively
Choice sweep string form renders bare booleans as 'True'/'False' and floats as '1.1'/'2.0' — exact string output format

New public name `Transformer` importable from hydra.core.override_parser.overrides_parser (or wherever Sweep types live), and its `encode` policy must map: bare values keep native type; quoted strings stay str; lists/dicts/complex values stringify via Hydra's element-to-string form

Exact encoded expectations for edge cases the instruction never specifies, e.g. `x=choice('1','2','3')` encodes to strings (quoted strings stay str), `1.1` stays float, `2.0` stays float, `'1.5'`/`'4'` stay strings, and lists of mixed values reproduce Hydra's compact string form like "[1,1.1,'2','a']"
The new method must be named `sweep_iterator` on `Override` and accept a keyword parameter `transformer=`; the instruction only suggests it as an example with naming 'up to you'

reasons: The instruction already proposes sweep_iterator with a caller-provided transformer and an encode-style Transformer, so the API shape and encoded outputs are covered. Only the import path/module of Transformer and the keyword name `transformer` are unstated, but both are natural choices an implementer would almost certainly land on.

The instruction proposes the names (sweep_iterator, Transformer, encode) but explicitly says naming is up to the implementer, so the exact identifier and keyword, plus the precise string flattening formats for lists/quoted strings, are only inferable from the hidden tests; they are conventional enough to grade as guessable.

The instruction intentionally leaves naming open, but the hidden tests pin the exact names `sweep_iterator(transformer=Transformer.encode)` and, more critically, exact per-value encode semantics (quoted strings stay str, lists stringify in Hydra's compact form, mixed bool/int/float passthrough) that are not derivable from the issue text.
